newsitem.title: UK: Sainsbury offers banking to regain market share.
newsitem.headline: Sainsbury offers banking to regain market share.

text.p: British supermarket group J. Sainsbury Plc launched its Sainsbury's Bank joint venture Wednesday in a move aimed at regaining its position as market leader in the highly competitive grocery business.
Sainsbury's Bank, owned 55 percent by Sainsbury and 45 percent by Bank of Scotland, will offer an Instant Access account with 5.75 percent annual interest and Visa credit cards.
Sainsbury is hoping that the bank will enhance customer loyalty and give an added marketing thrust to its brand, company spokesman Dominic Fry said.

Sainsbury has been struggling for the past year to regain its position as market leader in Britain's grocery industry. The chain was forced into launching a loyalty card last summer after the success of ClubCard helped rival Tesco overtake Sainsbury's market share.
Customers of the new Sainsbury's Bank will also gain extra points under Sainsbury's Reward loyalty scheme.
Sainsbury is the first of the big four British supermarkets to launch a banking service, although Tesco has plans with Royal Bank of Scotland and Safeway with Abbey National.
Sainsbury is hoping the banking facility will persuade more people to shop, and spend more money, at its supermarkets. But analysts said it could stir up competition swiftly.
"If the bank is successful, there will be a response from other supermarkets or retail banks and then the conversion of customers could slow," one analyst said.
Sainsbury said its earnings would be unaffected by the move since Sainsbury's Bank will operate as a separate entity.
